subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence: data location and erase-proof request (ZenithPay)
messages:
From: Claire D'Souza <audit@zenithpay.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <procurement@zenithpay.com>, ops@zenithpay.com
Date: 2026-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 evidence request — residency and deletion proofs

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our vendor SOC 2 review we need concrete artifacts showing how Redwood handles data residency, retention, and deletion for tenant-scoped data. High level answers are fine, but we also need: 

- A map of where PII and tenant data may persist (primary region, replicas, backups, caches).
- The technical deletion workflow (what background jobs run, and their IDs/outputs).
- Evidence that deleted data is removed from backups/snapshots or a compensating control if it cannot be immediately removed.
- A sample deletion job run log and any attestations you produce for customers.

Can you provide the above by COB Wednesday? We will include it with our audit binder.

Regards,
Claire D'Souza
Senior Auditor, ZenithPay

--
Note: attaching a template spreadsheet with the fields we expect in each artifact request (we'll reference your files in the spreadsheet).

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-07-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence request — residency and deletion proofs

Claire —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick note on scope: when you say "PII and tenant data" can you confirm you want production customer tenant data footprint (what is stored in object stores, DB replicas, Kafka topics, in-memory caches, and archived snapshots), or a narrower set (only primary DB + S3)? I want to avoid sending overly broad sensitive artifacts.

Planned deliverables by Wednesday EOD (if that scope is ok):
- Residency CSV (region/cluster/role) with labels for primary/replica/backup/cache.
- A sanitized sample of a tenant erasure run log (job id + timestamps + objects marked deleted).
- Deletion control matrix (high-level description that references the jobs and compensating controls for backups/snapshots).
- Short attestation text that you can include in your binder.

We'll attach logs and give you signed attestation links. If you need raw logs with full object names we need an executed NDA addendum — otherwise we'll provide truncated object ids and job ids.

Naomi
Data Privacy Manager
Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SOC 2 evidence request — residency and deletion proofs

Looping infra and compliance —

Notes from triage: 
- Primary storage: customer tenant metadata and content live in the us-west-2 tenant DB cluster (encrypted at rest).
- Replicas: async replicas exist in us-west-2 and us-east-1 for failover; replicas are eventually consistent but are part of the deletion workflow (we run cascading deletes).
- Backups: nightly snapshots of the DB are retained for 90 days; S3 object lifecycle policies move older backup archives to cold storage for up to 1 year before purge (per backup retention TTL).
- Caches: KV caches (redis) have TTLs and are flushed as part of deletion runs; some long-lived cache entries may persist for short windows (minutes).

Action items for deliverables: 
1) Produce residency-heatmap CSV describing primary/replica/backup/cache with short notes on deletion propagation. (Naomi)
2) Export a sanitized tenant-erasure-job-log showing job id, start/end, row counts, and propagated delete steps. (Infra / Rishi)
3) Create a short PDF explaining the compensating control for immutable snapshot retention (if we cannot surgically remove an archived snapshot, we provide legal attestation and retention schedule tied to the customer's contract). (Marissa)

Rishi — can you pull the 2026-07-21 erasure run for sample tenant ID ZN-44 and sanitize? Send job log + run UUID. We need the job log standardized (timestamp, step, affected partitions, objects marked). Put a redaction banner on object keys.

Vivek
Director, Platform Reliability

--

Quick summary of the run for tenant ZN-44:
- Job UUID: 87A2-ERASE-20260721-0312
- Start: 2026-07-21T03:12:07Z
- Phases: lock-tenant -> mark-in-db -> kv-cache-invalidate -> replica-cascade -> s3-object-delete -> snapshot-flag (compensating) -> finalize -> audit-record-publish
- Rows marked: 12,384 (primary DB)
- Objects enqueued for deletion: 784 (S3 keys) — keys redacted as requested
- Replica verify: 2 nodes reported successful cascade within 14s average latency
- Snapshot note: nightly DB snapshots are immutable; the run flags affected snapshot IDs for legal attestation and schedules them for retention policy review. We include the snapshot IDs in the attestation link rather than raw keys.

I uploaded the sanitized log to the internal attestation bucket and attached a local copy for the email. Let me know if you need the raw run for legal review (that will require a least-privileged transfer process).

-Rishi

Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence request — residency and deletion proofs

Claire —

Please find the deliverables attached and linked below. We have sanitized logs and a concise control narrative that maps to SOC 2 deletion criteria and ISO requirements. Summary below: 

1) Residency map (attached: residency-heatmap-2026-07.csv) — shows primary DB cluster, replica locations, S3 buckets used for transient objects and backups, and cache clusters. Labels show which stores are subject to the erasure workflow versus compensating controls.

2) Sanitary job log (attached: tenant-erasure-job-log-20260721-0312.txt) — demonstrates an end-to-end erasure run for tenant ZN-44. Job UUID: 87A2-ERASE-20260721-0312. The log contains phase timestamps, row/object counts, and verification status from replica nodes. Keys are redacted; we can provide an escrowed raw file under an NDA.

3) Deletion control matrix (attached: deletion-control-matrix-2026-07.pdf) — maps the steps in the deletion workflow to our technical controls and the compensating control where immediate removal from immutable snapshots is not feasible (retention TTL + contractual attestation).

4) Attestation link: https://redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com/attestations/zenith/2026-07-erasure-report-id-87A2 — this contains signed metadata and the snapshot IDs referenced in the log.

A few clarifications we typically provide auditors: 
- Backups: We do not surgically rewrite immutable historical DB snapshots after an erasure; instead we flag snapshot IDs in the attestation and apply a contractual retention schedule. For customers requiring immediate removal from snapshot media we offer a private deployment option with access to on-premise data removal workflows.
- Caches and streaming pipelines: these are included in the cascade and TTLs ensure removal within the stated SLO windows.
- Legal attestation: we can provide a signed attestation for the erasure job and a timestamped list of snapshot IDs tied to your tenant contract.

If you want a short cover note mapping these artifacts to specific SOC 2 criteria (CC6.1 / CC6.2 style mapping), we can produce that quickly.

Are these sufficient for your binder or would you like an on-call walkthrough with Rishi to step through the job log live?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Data Privacy Manager, Redwood Inference
